board.name: Vermont Board of Medical Practice (Department of Health)

categoryMin.label: Category 1
categoryMin.reason: Category 1 is read as AMA PRA and AAPA Category 1 credit, the two the Board names for the controlled substance hours (Rule 32.4.3).

notes.text: To renew an active license a PA must have practiced as a PA within the last three years, or met the Board's requirements for updating knowledge and skills.

topics.label: Controlled substance prescribing, AMA PRA or AAPA Category 1 or board designated, each renewal

condition.field: Holds or uses a DEA registration
condition.question: Do you hold a DEA registration or have one pending?
condition.description: Vermont presumes DEA holders and applicants prescribe controlled substances.

agreement.text: A written practice agreement with a participating physician is filed with the Board before practice and reviewed during the 90 days before each renewal, with the review documented in writing and signed by both. A new agreement reaches the Board before practice with a new employer.

unverified: Whether the hospice, palliative care or pain management CME hour (Rule 24.1.5, written for physicians) applies to PAs
Whether online PA renewal still asks for proof of NCCPA certification

board.name: Vermont State Board of Nursing (Office of Professional Regulation, Secretary of State)

options.text: At least 400 hours of practice in the two years before renewal, or 960 hours in five years
20 hours of qualifying continuing education in the two years before renewal

ce.reason: APRN renewal requires current national APRN certification and APRN practice hours; no general CE hours are listed.

cycleYears.reason: Licenses are valid for fixed two-year periods.

practiceHours.label: At least 400 hours of APRN practice in the two years before renewal, or 960 hours in the five years before

topics.label: Controlled substance prescribing, each licensing period

condition.field: Holds a DEA registration, has one pending, or dispenses controlled substances
condition.question: Do you hold a DEA registration, have one pending, or dispense controlled substances?
condition.description: Vermont's controlled substance CE (Act 173) applies to APRNs with a DEA number or a pending application, or who dispense.

unverified: How the Office of Professional Regulation collects the APRN controlled substance attestation

agreement.text: During transition to practice (fewer than 24 months and 2,400 hours in the initial role and population focus) an APRN keeps signed and dated collaborative provider agreements and presents a current one at renewal. Once the transition is complete the APRN notifies the Board and may practice solo.
